record.title: xAI describes Grok 4.7's longer-horizon training and reports multi-hour task results
record.summary: In a September 21 release, xAI described Grok 4.7 as using a larger base than Grok 4.6, a longer reinforcement-learning run weighted toward harder multi-hour tasks, and training to understand the Grok Bot harness. The release reports Grok 4.7 scores across coding, office, terminal, legal, electrical-engineering and clinical benchmarks, including 37.6% on Terminal-Bench 4.0 versus 20.3% for Grok 4.6. These are company-reported results; the page does not provide test protocols, sample sizes or uncertainty.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: xAI says Grok 4.7 uses a larger base than Grok 4.6, a longer reinforcement-learning run weighted toward harder multi-hour problems, and training for native Grok Bot harness understanding.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: xAI reports 37.6% for Grok 4.7 xHigh versus 20.3% for Grok 4.6 High on Terminal-Bench 4.0, with results across additional listed benchmarks.

claims.label: NOT_ESTABLISHED
claims.text: The release does not establish that the stated training changes caused the reported benchmark differences or that results generalize beyond the listed evaluations.

evidence_gaps.description: The release does not disclose benchmark prompts, sample sizes, scoring protocols, run variance or uncertainty for the reported scores.
No independent reproduction was inspected for the benchmark comparisons or training-mechanism claims.

brief.importance_rationale: If accurate and generalizable, a longer RL run focused on multi-hour tasks combined with native harness training could influence frontier agent development and extended-work deployment decisions. The release is first-party and provides benchmark numbers, but does not disclose methods or establish the causal contribution of those training choices.
limitations: All model-training and benchmark performance statements are reported by the vendor; the release does not publish a test protocol, sample sizes, uncertainty or independent reproduction.
Several vendor-to-vendor comparisons use different effort settings or are presented without matched compute and cost, so the table does not establish a general ranking.
The release does not establish that longer-horizon RL or harness training caused the reported benchmark differences.
brief.summary: In a September 21 release, xAI described Grok 4.7 as using a larger base than Grok 4.6, a longer reinforcement-learning run weighted toward harder multi-hour tasks, and training to understand the Grok Bot harness. The release reports Grok 4.7 scores across coding, office, terminal, legal, electrical-engineering and clinical benchmarks, including 37.6% on Terminal-Bench 4.0 versus 20.3% for Grok 4.6. These are company-reported results; the page does not provide test protocols, sample sizes or uncertainty.

technical.claimed_result: The release reports 37.6% for Grok 4.7 xHigh versus 20.3% for Grok 4.6 High on Terminal-Bench 4.0, 46.3% versus 40.4% on CursorBench 4.0, 1,657 versus 1,546 on AA Briefcase v1.1, and results across additional listed benchmarks. xAI also claims improved verification and long-context management.
technical.compute_or_cost: The release lists starting token prices of $2 per million input tokens and $6 per million output tokens; it does not provide benchmark token, latency or compute consumption.
technical.demonstrated_result: The official release page documents the launch date, stated training changes, reported benchmark table, pricing and availability. No independent technical result is demonstrated by this source.
technical.implementation_status: xAI announced availability through Cursor, Grok Build, the Grok API, third-party harnesses, model routers and cloud platforms as of September 21, 2026.
technical.mechanism: xAI says the model uses a new larger base than Grok 4.6, receives a longer reinforcement-learning run on a harder task mix weighted toward multi-hour problems, and is trained to natively understand the Grok Bot harness.
technical.novelty: The announcement combines a longer multi-hour-task-weighted RL run with training for native Grok Bot harness understanding, alongside benchmark claims for extended work.
technical.regime: A vendor release reports product-level benchmark comparisons across coding, multi-hour office and terminal tasks, electrical engineering, legal and clinical reasoning. The listed Grok settings vary by benchmark and are not uniformly matched to other vendors.
technical.reproducibility: The release provides benchmark names and scores but no prompts, sample sizes, scoring details, uncertainty, protocol, model snapshots or independent reproductions.
technical.strongest_baseline: Grok 4.6 at the listed settings; on Terminal-Bench 4.0, xAI reports 37.6% for Grok 4.7 xHigh and 20.3% for Grok 4.6 High. These effort settings are not matched.

brief.title: xAI describes Grok 4.7's longer-horizon training and reports multi-hour task results
brief.why_it_matters: The release makes a concrete frontier-lab claim that longer-horizon training and native harness understanding are productized together, and publishes a multi-hour task comparison. If independently supported, these design choices could affect how labs train and serve agents for extended work; the release alone does not establish that the training changes caused the reported gains.

related.summary: The events concern distinct Grok releases: this Oct 23 update describes Grok Bot product actions and approval behavior; the Sep 21 record concerns Grok 4.7 model training and benchmark claims.

other.title: xAI says Grok Bot update adds credential Vault and broadens agent actions
other.summary: An October 23 changelog for Grok Bot v0.75.5 says Bots can store logins, payment cards and contact details in a Vault and fill them at sign-in or checkout. The update also adds email forwarding and says Auto Review asks less often for requested actions; requested email and Slack messages send after Auto Review allows them, while routine and other-turn sends remain drafts. These are vendor-described features, not independently tested outcomes. xAI documentation says payment confirmations still require user handoff and describes Auto Review as model-based.
